newsitem.title: UK: U.S. T-bond futures charts darken, 106-00 on cards.
newsitem.headline: U.S. T-bond futures charts darken, 106-00 on cards.

text.p: T-bond futures will head toward its 1996 lows over the coming months, with any rallies seen only as corrections amid a downtrend, technical anlaysts said on Friday.

"Medium-term, T-bonds are in deep trouble," said Anne Whitby, head of techncial analysis at 4CAST in London. "They will probably stay ranging for a while, but I'm looking for them to test the 106-00 area, around the 1996 lows, and break those."
At 1106 GMT, June T-bond futures were up 7/32 at 108-23/32 in afterhours electronic trade.

On continuation charts, T-bond futures reached a major peak at the end of 1995 and in early January 1996, forming a triple top at 121-20/32 on December 6, 1995, 122-4/32 on January 4, 1996 and 121-26/32 on January 19, 1996.
From there, the market fell about 16 points in six months to make an initial low at 106-2/32 on June 13, 1996 and then, dipping to 105-28/32 on July 8.
The June 1997 contract low is at 104-9/32, made on June 13 of last year.
"What we've been seeing since June last year is a corrective rally distribution pattern," said Whitby.
The contract rallied to 116-00 in early Decmeber 1996.

Shea Bennett, technical analyst at Trend Analysis in Battle, southeast England, agreed the market was still in a downtrend but expected it to trade in choppy ranges for the next few months between 108-16/32 and 111-00.

"For the next two or three months, it is going to be broadly neutral but with a lot of volatility," he said. "It has done enough damage over the past four or five months to eliminate any strong bullish potential that we did have towards the end of last year."
David Sneddon, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London, said any rallies would be seen only as corrections.
"We are looking for it to eventually break down and move to 106-2, 105-28," he said.
But not all analysts saw the contract strecthing as far as these lows. David Wood, an independant techncial analyst near London, said much depended on the Eurodollar contract.
He said he was impressed by last Friday's T-bond rally and the way September Eurodollar futures held above 93.81 and rallied strongly.

"But this week's price action, particularly yesterday's, has been disappointing and has rekindled the negative aspect," Wood said. "The longer-term negative will be confirmed by a break below 93.81 in the September Eurodollars. That opens up a move of at least 50 ticks to the downside."

Though September Eurodollars held 93.81, he said bonds were obviously under pressure and could drop towards a measured target on daily charts at 106-22. September Eurodollars were up two basis points at 93.92 on afterhours electronic trade.

"In isolation, you can look at the bonds and say they are negative and should go to 106-22, but it would be wrong not to have the Eurodollar picture in your mind as well," he said. "Any sort of rally in Eurodollars will be coming off a strong base and should probably drag the bonds up."

The 106-22 level is calculated by taking the extent of the fall from December 3's high at 116-00 to the 108-30 low on January 29 projected onto the high from February 18 at 113-25. It also coincdes with the low on September 19.
